body:
Buying vapes online means handing a stranger your money, your address and your age details, and trusting them to deliver a genuine product. Most stores are honest, and some are not, and the difference is rarely visible on the front page. This guide gives you a practical method for judging an online vape store before you order: twelve checks you can complete in a few minutes, what a good answer looks like, what red flags to watch for, how to test a store with a small question, how to protect your payment and what to do if something goes wrong. It is written for adults aged 21 and over. Nicotine is addictive, and nothing here is medical advice. We apply these checks to ourselves, and you should too.

## Why the checks matter
Vape products have a specific set of risks when bought online. Counterfeit devices exist, and fakes can have poor batteries. Some sellers ignore age and shipping rules. Some take payment and never ship. Some make health claims that no retailer is allowed to make. A few minutes of checking reduces these risks a great deal, and costs you nothing.

## Check 1: age verification
A responsible store verifies that you are an adult, with an age gate on the site and a signature requirement on delivery. Under federal rules, remote sales of vapor products need an adult signature, and carriers will check ID. A store that skips age checks is ignoring the law, and may ignore other rules. See [what 21+ age verification means](/blog/what-21-plus-age-verification-means/).

## Check 2: a real business behind it
Look for a legal business name, a physical address and working contact details. A store with only a contact form is harder to hold to account. For example, our legal operator is SV3 LLC, and our address and phone are published on the [contact page](/contact/). Search the address, and see whether it is plausible.

## Check 3: policies you can read
Shipping, returns, privacy and terms should be easy to find and written in plain language. Read them before you order. Look for processing times, carriers, return windows, restocking fees and refund methods. A store that hides its policies, or has none, is not one to trust with your money. See our [shipping](/shipping/), [refund](/refunds/) and [privacy](/privacy/) policies as examples.

## Check 4: legal awareness
A reputable store knows the rules for remote sales, including the PACT Act, and mentions them. It should not promise delivery to places where products are restricted. See [the PACT Act explained for vape buyers](/blog/pact-act-explained-for-vape-buyers/) and [state and local vape laws explained](/blog/state-and-local-vape-laws-explained/).

## Check 5: no health claims
Be cautious about any seller that says its products are good for you, less harmful than other options or endorsed by a health authority. Retailers should not make these claims. Look for a plain nicotine warning instead. Nicotine is addictive, and we make no health claims.

## Check 6: realistic prices
If a price is far below the going rate, ask why. Counterfeits, stolen goods and non-existent stock are common explanations. Compare similar products across several stores. See [how to spot counterfeit vapes](/blog/how-to-spot-counterfeit-vapes/) and [how to compare vape prices per puff](/blog/how-to-compare-vape-prices-per-puff/).

## Check 7: honest product pages
Good pages list brand, flavor, strength, puff count, battery and liquid details, and show the actual product. They avoid vague superlatives. They do not show fake countdowns or invented stock levels. See [how to read a vape product page](/blog/how-to-read-a-vape-product-page/).

## Check 8: real, attributable reviews
Reviews are useful when they are real. Be cautious about perfect scores with no names, and about stores that show the same review on every product. We do not invent reviews, ratings or statistics, and we show none where we have none.

## Check 9: a clear payment process
You should know what to pay, to whom and how you will be told it was received. Beware of sellers who ask for payment through unusual channels after you order, without explaining. Never send payment details in response to an unsolicited message. See [payment methods compared](/blog/payment-methods-compared/) and [how payment details reach you](/blog/how-payment-details-reach-you/). A store that accepts cryptocurrency should publish its public addresses and never ask for private keys.

## Check 10: order tracking and communication
After you order, you should get an order ID and a way to see status. Tracking should be provided when shipped. See [how to track your order](/blog/how-to-track-your-order/).

## Check 11: responsive support
Send a simple question before you buy, such as the strength of a product or the shipping time to your state. A prompt, specific answer is a good sign. A slow, vague or pushy one is not. See [how to contact support](/blog/how-to-contact-support/).

## Check 12: no pressure
Reputable stores do not rush you, threaten that prices will vanish in minutes or ask you to move to private channels to pay. If you feel pushed, stop.

## A quick scoring method
Give the store one point for each check it passes. Ten or more is a good sign. Seven to nine means ask questions before ordering. Below seven, look elsewhere. The method is rough, but it makes you look at each point instead of trusting a pleasant design.

## Testing with a small order
If you are unsure, test with a small order of a product you want anyway. Note how long processing takes, whether tracking arrives, how the packaging looks and how support responds. Remember that our minimum order is $100, and other stores may have different rules.

## Protecting your payment
Use a method you understand. Keep screenshots and confirmations. Do not share card numbers, passwords or private keys in messages. If you pay by cryptocurrency, copy the address carefully, send the exact amount and keep the transaction hash. See [how we detect your crypto payment](/blog/how-we-detect-your-crypto-payment/).

## If something goes wrong
Contact the store first, with your order ID and clear photos. Read the refund policy for what applies. Keep all messages. If the store does not respond, consider your payment provider's dispute process, where one exists, and report suspected fraud to the relevant authority.

## Red flags in one list
- No age verification.
- No address or phone number.
- No policies.
- Health claims.
- Prices that are too good to be true.
- Pressure to pay quickly.
- Requests for private keys, passwords or card numbers in messages.
- Reviews with no names, all perfect.

## Frequently asked questions in depth
### Is a professional-looking site proof of legitimacy?
No. Designs are easy to copy. Check the substance.

### How long should shipping take?
It depends on the store. Ours: 24 to 72 business hours of processing, then about 3 to 18 business days depending on your region.

### Should I worry about adult signature?
No. It is a legal requirement, and a sign that the store follows the rules.

### Can I ask a store for proof?
You can ask about batch details, contact information and policies.

### Where do I report a scam?
To your payment provider and to consumer protection authorities.

## Shop
Browse [disposable vapes](/shop/disposables/) and [vape juice](/shop/vape-juice/). All products are for adults aged 21 and over, and nicotine is addictive.

## Applying the checks to a real example
Imagine you are comparing two stores for a 30,000-puff disposable. Store A shows a legal business name and a street address, has an age gate, links its shipping and refund policies, lists strength and battery details on the product page, says that an adult must sign for delivery and offers three payment methods, with instructions that arrive after you order. It answers your pre-sale question within a day, with specific details. Store B has a slick design, a price 40 percent below everyone else, no address, no policy pages and a request to pay by an unusual method as soon as you click. On the checklist, Store A scores eleven or twelve, and Store B scores two or three. You do not need to guess about the second store, because the checks tell you.

## Keeping your own records
Keep a note of every order: the store, date, order ID, payment method and amount, a screenshot of the product page and any messages. If a problem arises, records make it easier to resolve. They also help you compare stores over time, because you will see which ones were clear and prompt and which were not.

## A final word on trust
No checklist is perfect, and an honest store can still make a mistake. What matters is how the store behaves when it does. A store that publishes its terms, answers questions and fixes errors is one you can work with, and one that hides, deflects or goes silent is one to leave. Use the checks, trust your judgment and start small if you are unsure.

## Questions worth asking before you order
Send a short message and judge the reply. Ask what the nicotine strength of a product is, whether it is rechargeable and how long delivery to your state usually takes. Ask who the legal operator of the store is and where it is based. A good store answers each question directly, without pressure, and does not mind that you asked. If the answer is vague, late or dodges the question, take that as information. You can ask us the same questions through the [contact page](/contact/), and we will answer from our own policies and product data.

faq.q: How do I know an online vape store is reputable?
faq.a: Check age verification, a real business address, readable policies, legal awareness, no health claims, realistic prices, honest product pages, a clear payment process, tracking and responsive support.

faq.q: Is a low price a red flag?
faq.a: Often yes. Prices far below the going rate can mean counterfeits or non-existent stock.

faq.q: Why do stores require an adult signature?
faq.a: Federal rules for remote sales of vapor products require it, and it is a sign that a store follows the rules.

faq.q: What payment red flags should I watch for?
faq.a: Requests for private keys, passwords or card numbers in messages, unusual channels with no explanation and pressure to pay quickly.

faq.q: How can I test a store?
faq.a: Send a specific question first, and note how quickly and clearly it is answered. A small order can also test processing and tracking.
Contact the store with your order ID, read its refund policy, keep your messages and use your payment provider's dispute process if needed.
